title: Max at Restaurant Night
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: "Guess where we are having dinner tonight?" asks Grandma. "Pizza My Heart! It is a McKinley Restaurant Night." Max does a happy dance. But what is a Restaurant Night?

Grandma explains. On Restaurant Night, a restaurant gives part of the money from dinner to the McKinley PTA. The PTA uses the money for special things at school, like field trips, art supplies, and fun events. "So eating pizza helps our school?" asks Max. "Exactly," says Grandma.
At the restaurant, Max sees lots of McKinley families. Lupe is there with her big brother, and Kai waves from a booth. It feels like a school party, but with pizza.

When they order, Grandma says, "We are here for McKinley." The cashier writes it down so the school gets its share. Max orders a slice with pepperoni and a slice with pineapple, because Max cannot decide.

On the way home, Max does some math. "If lots of families eat pizza tonight, the school gets lots of money. That means more art supplies!" Grandma laughs. "You are a very smart Bulldog, and a very full one."
